recurring_symptoms: don't know how much to set aside for quarterly taxes
spreadsheet formulas break when I edit them
expense categories don't map to Schedule C
root_problems: No withholding, quarterly estimated taxes and Schedule C categories are confusing; generic templates break or don't match the tax regime.
desired_outcomes: Invoice, track income/expenses, and know what to set aside for taxes without panic at year-end.
solution_weaknesses: Categories don't map to Schedule C
Generic — not tuned to a specific 1099 trade
unmet_needs: Correct US SE-tax + quarterly-estimate logic that a non-accountant trusts
solution_gaps: robust-but-not-overwhelming middle ground (templates are too simple OR too complex)
formulas that don't break on edit
contradictions: Free 1099 templates are abundant — risk of a 'free-information' problem for the generic version.
Etsy SEO is owned by high-volume generalist shops — the marketing problem may exceed the product problem.
A subset of freelancers offload this entirely to an accountant and won't buy a tool.
opportunity_assessment: Strong, evidence-backed recurring problem with PROVEN willingness-to-pay ($9-25; RunTheCalc 2.2k sales @ ~$17) and a clear correctness+specificity gap. Main risk is distribution, not demand: incumbents are fragmented but own Etsy search, and free templates compete. Wedge = a specific US 1099 sub-niche + verifiable correctness (SE tax, quarterly estimates, Schedule C) + an off-Etsy distribution angle.
